articles.title: Dollar Rangebound Ahead of U.S. Midterm Elections as Markets Weigh Global Drivers
articles.intro: The US dollar traded rangebound and slipped slightly ahead of the upcoming congressional elections, while major currencies displayed mixed movements. Meanwhile, traders kept a close watch on shifting global fundamentals, including ongoing developments in energy and monetary policy expectations.

sections.p: Market sentiment remains cautious as participants navigate a busy macroeconomic calendar alongside shifting political and technological landscapes. The US dollar slipped slightly ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, while the euro gained ground and the Japanese yen eased. Concurrently, the Canadian dollar slipped from a six-week high as an oil retreat offset the weaker dollar, and sterling found support from Iran diplomacy bets. Safe-haven discussions also surfaced around gold and alternative assets as wider market sectors absorb recent geopolitical and tech-sector headlines.

The primary focus for foreign exchange markets centers on political developments and upcoming central bank decisions. U.S. congressional elections are currently underway, keeping the dollar generally rangebound. Elsewhere, attention turns to the Reserve Bank of Australia, which is scheduled to deliver its cash rate decision and monetary policy statement with a forecast of 4.85%. Later in the week, the Bank of England will release its monetary policy report, summary, and official bank rate vote, with a rate forecast pointing to 4.00%. These central bank trajectories, alongside persistent expectations regarding rate hikes, continue to dictate broader currency flows.

Major currency pairs continue to print predominantly sideways trends across current technical boards. EUR/USD trades near 1.1216 with an RSI of 54.5, sitting between support at 1.113 and resistance at 1.1269. GBP/USD holds at 1.34194 with an RSI of 69.2, pressing against its resistance level. USD/JPY trades near 157.9 with an RSI of 47.9, supported at 156.8 and capped near 158.6. USD/CAD sits at 1.3974 showing an oversold RSI of 15.9, while NZD/USD remains in a downtrend at 0.56265. Commitment of Traders data shows net positioning remaining heavily short for the euro and Australian dollar, while net longs persist in Japanese yen and gold.

Traders should closely monitor the unfolding results of the U.S. congressional elections and their immediate impact on dollar liquidity. Upcoming top-tier risk events include the RBA rate statement and press conference, followed later in the week by New Zealand employment data and the Bank of England's rate decision and Governor Bailey's speech. Keeping an eye on technical support and resistance levels across major pairs will be essential as these key data points cross the wire.
